rationale: M49 ledger G7, closed 2026-09-15. Groovy string interpolation was invisible to the graph: the grammar extends Java, so it inherited Java's `string_fragment` (`token.immediate(prec(1, /[^"\\]+/))` — everything except `"` and `\`, which INCLUDES `$` and `{`) and Java's `string_interpolation` (`'\{' … '}'`, Java's text-block form, which Groovy source never contains). No interpolated expression could reach the analyzer: `${user.name}` produced NO read, `${obj.method()}` NO call, and the raw-nested-quote subset did not even parse. Corpus size, source-matched over grails-core @ a83f8748 (7,701 groovy-surface files): 2,115 files (27.5%) contain interpolation, 13,830 sites, each contributing 0 relationships. MEASURED PRE/POST ON THIS EXACT FILE, identical instrument, only `wasm/tree-sitter-groovy.wasm` differing: PRE 8 symbols / 15 relationships, POST 9 / 22 — the missing symbol is `typeMap` (the parenthesised ARRAY-TYPE map key, also closed by this round) and the missing edges are the six pinned below. The fixture is one file so every control sits beside its claim: the CONTRACT is (a) a FREE name in interpolation is a READ, (b) a name the current callable BINDS is not a graph node and must NOT be read, (c) a member or call inside a string behaves EXACTLY as the same expression outside it (so `registry.lookup("G7")` emits its `calls` edge and does NOT additionally leak a `uses` for its callee), and (d) SINGLE-quoted strings never interpolate. Both directions are asserted: expectRelationships catches a dropped branch, forbidRelationships catches a missing gate — which is what the naive fixes produce (reading `$count` where `count` is a parameter, or `$it` inside a closure, fabricates an edge for a name that has no symbol at all). `authoredBeforeAnalyzerRun` is false because the expectation is read off the corrected emission; the pre-fix measurement above is the provenance.

expectSymbols.name: typeMap
expectSymbols.note: PRE-FIX this symbol did not exist: `[(Byte[]): v]` was an ERROR and the class body's tail was lost with it

expectRelationships.note: the `${…}` long form: a free member name is a READ
the `$name` short form in the SAME string — both syntaxes, one line, so they cannot diverge unnoticed
`${user.name}`: the member is read by the field-access walk, whose line is the leaf's
`${user.notify()}`: the CALL is emitted by the call walk — the same edges inside a string as outside it
a free read in a method that also contains a closure, so the binding climb cannot stop at the closure

SLASHY: the `${templateName}` inside /…/ is the same read it would be inside "…" — one contract for every interpolating form, both syntaxes pinned on one line (shape copied from GspTagSourceMacro.groovy:70)
the raw-nested-quote string (`selected="selected"` inside the `${}` body) now parses, and its inner call is real
CONTROL: the slashy method's ordinary call still comes from the call walk
CONTROL: a call on the same line outside any interpolation, unchanged by the fix
the array-type map key parses, so the member survives — pre-fix the whole tail of the class was lost

forbidRelationships.note: a name render BINDS with `def local` — a read here is the fabrication every `"$local"` in the corpus would produce
a parameter of render: bound, so not a graph node
a parameter again — the RECEIVER of `user.name` is not itself a read
bound by a `def` in the nested closure; the climb must pass through the closure AND still suppress it
a closure's implicit `it` is bound without being written down — the single most common Groovy interpolation, and the one a naive fix turns into thousands of phantom edges
a callee is not a read — java/kotlin/scala and the #852 ruling all suppress it
the slashy ANCHOR control: `/end$/` must stay literal — a read here means the fix interpolates regex end-anchors and would corrupt every /x$/ pattern in the corpus
the callee of `className.isEmpty()` is the call walk's, so it leaks no read
the BOUND slashy case: `className` is the method's own parameter, so a `$name` in a slashy string must not read it — the binding test governs both string forms
NEGATIVE CONTROL: `'${templateField} $style'` is SINGLE-quoted, so Groovy never interpolates it — a read here means the fix reads the text of a plain string
a member read emitted as a CALL (the #851 class, re-asserted where a string is involved)
